ABSTRACT
Phishing websites imitate legitimate websites to steal sensitive user information such
as passwords and financial data. These fake sites are designed to look trustworthy,
making it difficult for users to distinguish between real and malicious websites. As a
result, many users unknowingly share their confidential information, leading to
security and financial risks. To address this problem, a machine learning–based
system is developed that analyzes various URL features to detect phishing websites.
The system extracts important characteristics from the URL and uses the Random
Forest algorithm to classify websites as either phishing or legitimate based on learned
patterns. The system then predicts whether a website is safe or suspicious and
displays the result to the user. This helps users identify potentially harmful websites
and avoid possible cyber threats.

INTRODUCTION
Phishing is a common cyberattack in which attackers create
fake websites to trick users into revealing sensitive information.
These websites often closely resemble legitimate ones, making
them difficult for users to identify. Traditional detection
techniques are not always effective in detecting newly created
phishing websites. However, machine learning can analyze
patter ns in URLs and identify suspicious characteristics,
helping to detect phishing attempts more effectively. It can also
learn from large datasets and improve its accuracy over time.
This approach enables faster and more reliable detection of
potentially harmful websites.
